newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude off on technical weakness, gasoline.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude off on technical weakness, gasoline.

text.p: NYMEX crude turned lower Thursday afternoon when it failed to break key technical resistance of $26.80, crude's post-Gulf War high, while losses in gasoline weighed on the oil complex generally.
"Crude hit good resistance at $26.80 and went back," said Warren Tashnek, president of Fimat USA Futures in Houston.
At 1459 EST, February crude was off 16 cents at $26.46 a barrel while February gasoline was off 1.04 cents a gallon at 71.15 cents.
"There are a lot of cargoes coming over carryng gasoline, so gasoline is taking a back seat," said Tashnek.

There was talk of gasoline cargoes arriving from Europe to the New York Harbor in late January. The talk of imports follows inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute Tuesday showing major rise in gasoline stocks.

Ample supplies near term put prompt gasoline into contango several times during the session. Contango is when the contract for nearest delivery becomes cheaper than the contracts for the proceeding periods.
Gasoline pushed February heating oil off 0.43 cent at 73.00 cents a gallon.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
